implementation_summary: Created e2e/tests/forget-device-sibling.spec.ts following S6's structural pattern. The spec uses a describe.serial block with a Date.now() group name (AC-E2E-2). Three contexts: A1 (sibling-forgetter, slot 'sibling-a1'), A2 (target, slot 'sibling-a2', same bunker as A1), B (observer, slot 'observer', distinct bunker). Authentication order: B first, A2 second, A1 last (so A1 is group admin). A1 creates the group, invites B by npub, waits 8s for auto-invite to pull in A2's KP (same-npub multi-device flow), then A2 and B join. Core test: A1 opens Settings → Devices, locates A2's non-local row via data-testid='device-row'[data-local='false'] filtered by slot text (with a fallback to first non-local row), clicks the sibling-forget button and confirm button. Assertions: (1) leafIndexesFor(pageA1, groupId, pubkeyA) drops to 1 (A1's own leaf remains); (2) same from pageB perspective confirming global commit propagation; (3) pageA1.__notestrTestForgottenSlots() contains 'sibling-a2'. No kind-5 relay assertion per Design Decision #2. TypeScript compiles cleanly for the new file (npx tsc --noEmit produces no errors in forget-device-sibling.spec.ts; two pre-existing errors in S3's forget-device.test.ts are not introduced by this story).
caveats: Q-POSTIMPL-2 PARTIAL sev 3, confidence 0.5: 8s settle after inviteByNpub is a heuristic mirroring the shipped multi-device-cross-npub.spec.ts pattern. Empirical validation deferred to Step 6 e2e run. If selectGroup times out, increase to 12s or replace with expect.poll(leafIndexesFor).toHaveLength(2).
